title: Papyrus Lint project configuration
description: A papyrus-lint.yaml / papyrus-lint.yml file at a project root. Every key is optional; omitted keys fall back to the defaults documented here and in the generated shared/configuration/papyrus-lint.default.yaml artifact. The loader currently ignores unknown keys, but this schema sets additionalProperties to false so editors can flag typos.

game.description: Game whose Papyrus dialect and runtime APIs the project targets.

compiler_path.description: Path to PapyrusCompiler.exe, or null/omit to auto-detect it.

additional_script_roots.description: Extra directories (relative to the project root, or absolute) to search for .psc files, besides scripts/source and source/scripts. Used for linting, cross-script resolution, and the compiler -i path.

lookup_script_roots.description: Extra directories searched only as a fallback when resolving other scripts for analysis (argument/return types, Extends, autocompletion). Scripts found only here are never linted, and these directories are ignored by conflicting-script-versions.

compile_check.description: Also run PapyrusCompiler.exe (into a throwaway temporary directory) as part of linting a .psc, reporting its errors alongside the lint engine. Requires compiler_path to be set or auto-detected.

strict_achlist_scope.description: When true, restrict cross-script resolution and conflicting-script-versions to an achlist's listed entries only. When false (the default), parent directories of listed entries are also search roots.

semicolon.description: Whether lines are required to end in a semicolon (true) or must not (false).

indentation.description: Expected indentation style, read by the indentation lint and automatic fix.

indentation_width.description: Spaces per indentation level. Used only when indentation is space. The engine clamps this to 1..16.

max_line_length.description: Non-negative integer; maximum characters allowed on one line

identifier_casing.description: Casing style declared identifiers must match (functions, events, properties, states, parameters, locals).

cyclomatic_complexity_warning.description: Cyclomatic complexity at which the cyclomatic-complexity lint reports a warning.

cyclomatic_complexity_error.description: Cyclomatic complexity at which the cyclomatic-complexity lint reports an error. A value below cyclomatic_complexity_warning is treated as equal to it.

type_casing.description: Casing convention for a script's declared type name (the identifier following ScriptName).

named_arguments.description: How strongly a positional call argument should be passed by name instead.

min_wait_interval.description: Interval/duration argument a Utility.Wait / RegisterForUpdate / RegisterForSingleUpdate / RegisterForUpdateGameTime / RegisterForSingleUpdateGameTime call can go below before short-wait-interval flags it.

magic_numbers.description: Whether the magic-numbers lint also flags Wait/RegisterFor* interval arguments (strict) or leaves them unflagged (loose).

fail_on_warning.description: Whether the CLI treats a warning-level diagnostic as a non-zero exit. Has no effect on the desktop app.

fail_on_info.description: Whether the CLI treats an info-level diagnostic as a non-zero exit. Has no effect on the desktop app.

bool_like_int.description: Whether strict-boolean accepts the Int literals 1 and 0 used directly as If/ElseIf/While conditions.

treat_form_as_bool_for_returns.description: Whether return-types accepts a non-array Form value returned from a Bool function, relying on Papyrus's implicit None/existing Form conversion.

assume_auto_properties_filled.description: Whether none-form-usage treats a script-level Auto/AutoReadOnly property as already filled in by the time a function runs, instead of possibly None.

rules.description: Per-rule enable/disable switches. Omitted keys use each rule's default.

line_length.description: Flags lines that exceed the configured maximum character count.

trailing_whitespace.description: Flags lines that end with trailing spaces or tabs.

final_newline.description: Requires non-empty files to end with exactly one newline.

comma_spacing.description: Requires whitespace after commas in argument lists.

forbidden_functions.description: Flags calls to functions that are usually unintentional performance bottlenecks. `Debug.*` already behind a simple debug-flag If (e.g. `If IsDebugMode`) is left unflagged.

deprecated_functions.description: Flags calls to compiled-in deprecated functions or project functions marked `; @deprecated`, and recommends supported alternatives where available.

formid_hex_notation.description: Flags a FormID literal compared against GetFormID() or passed to Game.GetFormFromFile that isn't written in hexadecimal.

get_form_from_file_skyrim_esm.description: Flags Game.GetFormFromFile(id, "Skyrim.esm"), which is exactly what Game.GetForm(id) already does.

get_form_from_file_load_index.description: Flags a hex FormID literal passed to Game.GetFormFromFile that carries a non-zero load index, or leading zero digits, neither of which Game.GetFormFromFile ever uses.

slow_functions.description: Flags calls to functions that have a faster equivalent available; the fix applies the supplied replacement.

unused_getter.description: Flags standalone calls to functions whose names begin with Get if the returned value is unused.

unused_nodiscard.description: Flags discarded results of functions marked ; @nodiscard.

unused_property.description: Flags Property declarations whose name is never referenced anywhere else in the script.

semicolon.description: Requires a trailing semicolon on each non-empty line or forbids terminal semicolons, according to the selected setting.

float_int_conversion.description: Flags a Float value declared, assigned, returned, or passed as an argument into an Int-typed slot without an explicit as Int cast.

int_division_to_float.description: Flags an Int/Int division declared, assigned, returned, or passed as an argument into a Float-typed slot, since Papyrus truncates the division before it ever widens into the Float (e.g. Float f = 1 / 2 yields 0.0, not 0.5). A constant division that divides evenly (e.g. 72 / 8) isn't flagged.

strict_boolean.description: Flags conditions that rely on Papyrus treating a none-boolean as a boolean. Allows the literal 1/0 as bool-like by default (configurable).

argument_types.description: Flags call-site arguments whose type doesn't match the callee's declared parameter type.

return_types.description: Flags statements whose value's type doesn't match the enclosing function's declared return type.

function_override.description: Informs about a function declared on this script that shares its name with a function declared on the script it extends.

argument_naming.description: Flag a function declared on this script whose parameter name doesn't match (case-insensitively) the corresponding parameter of the same-named function declared on the script it Extends.

argument_override_types.description: Flags a function or event whose parameter count or types don't match the same-named function declared on the script it Extends.

numeric_comparison.description: Flags implicit comparisons between ints and floats that rely on Papyrus doing type conversions.

indentation.description: Flags lines whose indentation doesn't match the configured style/width.

cyclomatic_complexity.description: Flags functions/events whose cyclomatic complexity exceeds a configurable threshold. A configured error threshold below the warning one is treated as equal to it.

unreachable_statement.description: Flags statements that follow a Return.

static_condition.description: Flags conditions that resolve the same every time due to this likely being a mistake.

unreachable_elseif.description: Flags an ElseIf whose condition can never be true because an earlier branch already covers it.

division_by_zero.description: Flags divisions by zero where they are likely to happen.

empty_body.description: Flags seemingly useless loops and conditional bodies, since they are likely a mistake.

empty_event_handler.description: Flags a completely empty Event in the empty/default state. Empty handlers inside a named State are left alone, since those often intentionally mute an inherited or engine event.

duplicate_conditional_body.description: Flags consecutive If/ElseIf/Else branches whose bodies are the same, since that usually means a branch was copied and left unchanged.

unused_local_variable.description: Flags a local variable inside a function/event whose value is never read: either it's never referenced again at all or only written to.

variable_used_before_assignment.description: Flags a local variable declared without an initial value that's read before it's ever assigned one, since it then still holds its default value. A comparison against that same default (None, 0, 0.0, False, or "") is treated as a deliberate gate, not a flagged read, even when joined by && or || to a further operand that only runs once the gate rules out the default.

none_form_usage.description: Flags a member/method access on a local variable or script-level property that's still known to be None. Set assume_auto_properties_filled to stop assuming an unset Auto/AutoReadOnly property starts out None; it's still tracked once code assigns it None directly.

member_chain_none_usage.description: Flags a member/method access whose receiver is itself a member or call (e.g. a.GetLinkTo(...).Kill()), which none-form-usage skips. Opt-in: intermediate results are not proven None, so this is noisier than none-form-usage.

local_variable_shadowing.description: Flags a local variable whose name matches (case-insensitively) a Property or a plain script-level variable declared on the same script.

parameter_reassignment.description: Flags a function/event parameter assigned a new value anywhere in its own body.

chain_whitespace.description: Flags a space or tab immediately before or after a member/method access.

exclamation_spacing.description: Flags a negation operator not followed by exactly one space. In a chained negation such as !!bReady, only the final ! requires a trailing space.

identifier_casing.description: Flags a declared function/event, property, state, parameter, or local/script variable whose name doesn't match the configured style.

type_casing.description: Flags a script's declared type name if it doesn't follow the configured convention. Ignores a leading acronym prefix (e.g. CreationKit's own fragment names or a mod's acronym prefix), which can't be renamed.

named_arguments.description: Flags a positional call argument that the configured setting prefers to see passed by Papyrus's named-argument syntax instead; the fix inserts the matching parameter name ahead of it.

operator_spacing.description: Requires exactly one space on either side of logical operators.

assignment_operator_spacing.description: Requires exactly one space on either side of =, +=, -=, *=, /=, and %=.

property_sorting.description: Flag declaration that isn't sorted by type and then alphabetically by name, or that isn't declared immediately after the ScriptName line, before any variable, function, or state declaration.

explicit_return.description: Flags a typed function/event with a code path that falls off the end of its body without a Return.

unchecked_form_parameter.description: Flags a member/method access on a Form-typed function parameter that hasn't yet been confirmed non-None in that path.

unchecked_array_element.description: Flags a member/method access on a constant-indexed array element (e.g. act[2].Kill()) that hasn't yet been confirmed non-None in that path. Disabled by default, same as the Form parameter check above.

unchecked_cast.description: Flags a member/method access on the result of an As cast before that result has been checked against None. Never flags CreationKit's own fragment boilerplate cast (e.g. Actor akSpeaker = akSpeakerRef as Actor).

useless_downcast.description: Flags a cast to a parent type that has no actual value and just makes reading a bit harder.

impossible_cast.description: Flags an As cast proven to never succeed, e.g. Weapon b = a as Weapon where a is an Armor, since Armor and Weapon are unrelated types. Only flagged once both types are confirmed to resolve to a known root.

unresolved_script.description: Flags script name references that can't be resolved against the configured source directories.

non_global_function_call.description: Flags a ScriptName.Function() call whose target function resolves but isn't declared Global, since Papyrus's static call syntax can only reach Global functions.

member_access.description: Flags access to a function or property whose @private or @protected visibility does not permit access from the current script.

register_for_update_in_on_update.description: Flags RegisterForUpdate / RegisterForUpdateGameTime called inside OnUpdate / OnUpdateGameTime, which stacks another repeating timer every tick; use RegisterForSingleUpdate (or the GameTime variant) instead.

static_function_call_via_instance.description: Flags a Global function called through an object reference (e.g. akRef.MyGlobalHelper()) instead of ScriptName.MyGlobalHelper(); Papyrus allows it, but it can read as a mistake. Self/Parent are never flagged.

short_wait_interval.description: Flags Waits and RegisterFor(Single)Update(GameTime) if the time is smaller than a configured amount.

state_function_signature.description: Flags a function or event in a State whose parameters or return type don't match its empty-state declaration.

goto_state.description: Flags states that are undefined, likely because of typos.

get_state_comparison.description: Flags a GetState() == "Name"/!= "Name" comparison against an undefined state, since it then always evaluates to the same result instead of raising an error.

unused_state.description: Flags named states that are neither Auto nor targeted by a GoToState call.

too_many_states.description: Flags a file if the number of states exceeds the possible 128.

multiple_auto_states.description: Reports multiple Auto states in one script as an error, or multiple across its ancestry as a warning.

conflicting_script_versions.description: Flags byte-different copies of the same script in separate source directories. Identity is the path under the script root, so User/Foo.psc does not conflict with Other/Foo.psc.

stale_compiled_output.description: Flags a .psc file whose compiled .pex is older than the script itself, usually meaning it was edited and never recompiled.

script_filename_mismatch.description: Flags a .psc file whose declared ScriptName doesn't match its path under the script root, aside from casing. An unqualified name is the file stem; Fallout 4 / Starfield A:B:C must end in A/B/C.psc after any layout folders the name does not include.

unused_disable.description: Flags unknown @disable/@disable-file rule ids and directives that suppress no diagnostic. Disabled by default.

magic_numbers.description: Flags numeric literals used directly instead of through a named constant, property, or local variable. -1, 0 and 1 are never flagged. Loose mode (default) exempts Wait/RegisterFor(Single)Update(GameTime) intervals, Strict checks them too. Disabled by default.

native_function_usage.description: Flags a Native function/event whose name isn't one of the base game's own, a sign it needs SKSE/F4SE or another native extension. Disabled by default.

repeated_getvalue.description: Flags GetValue() called on the same global more than once across an If/ElseIf chain's conditions, since it can be cached in a local variable instead. Disabled by default.

global_variable_setvalue.description: Flags a SetValue/SetValueInt call that doesn't provably change the value: a branch writing back the exact value its own GetValue() == literal condition just confirmed, or an Else branch writing a literal with no check ruling out that value already being current. Disabled by default.

global_variable_increment.description: Flags gv.SetValue(gv.GetValue() + x), since GlobalVariable's native Mod(x) call does the same thing in one call instead of two; the fix rewrites the call to gv.Mod(x).

setvalue_in_loop.description: Flags a SetValue/SetValueInt call inside a While loop's body, since it then runs on every iteration; not flagged if the loop also calls Utility.Wait/RegisterForUpdate.

invariant_loop_condition.description: Flags a While loop whose condition depends on a local variable/parameter that's never assigned anywhere in its own body, since it can then never stop or never run.

script_name_collision.description: Flags a script-level Property or variable whose name matches the script it's declared in, since Papyrus fails to compile it.

array_bounds.description: Flags a literal index into a local array that falls outside the constant size it was declared with (e.g. new Float[3] followed by a[5]), since Papyrus silently no-ops the access instead of raising an error.

array_size_range.description: Flags, as an error, a new array whose own literal size falls outside 0 to 128, since Papyrus hard-caps a script-created array at 128 elements and a negative size makes no sense; doesn't apply to array Properties or natively-returned arrays, so those aren't checked against it.

array_used_before_new.description: Flags indexing or member access (.Length, Find, Add, …) on a local array that is still known to be None because it was never created with New (or assigned another array).

readonly_property_write.description: Flags an assignment to a property declared AutoReadOnly, since Papyrus rejects that at compile time. Matches the property's bare name or Self.PropertyName; a bare name shadowed by a same-named local/parameter is left alone.

default_property_value.description: Flags a Bool/Int/Float/String Auto/AutoReadOnly property with no explicit default value, since it then silently falls back to Papyrus's own implicit per-type default instead of a value the author chose. Disabled by default.

unguarded_self_recursion.description: Flags a function/event that calls itself with nothing that could ever skip the recursive call, since it then recurses unconditionally until the call stack is exhausted. Conservative: a self-call nested inside an If/While is always left alone, a top-level While always disqualifies the function, and a top-level If only counts as a guard when it actually contains a Return somewhere within it — an If with no Return does nothing to stop the call and is still flagged. A GoToState to a different state that declares its own handler for the same function/event, before the self-call, counts as a guard too, covering the vanilla save-compatibility idiom. Exception: if every branch of an If/Elseif/Else covering every path directly calls itself, it's flagged anyway, since it recurses no matter which branch runs.

self_assignment.description: Flags a plain = assignment whose right side is the exact same reference as its own target (e.g. a = a, Self.Foo = Self.Foo), since it can never change the value and is almost always a mistake. Only a bare name or a chain of member accesses is compared this way; calls, indexes, and compound assignments (+=, ...) are never flagged.

debug_side_effects.description: Flags a call to a side-effecting function nested inside any Debug.* argument list, since that call only runs when the debug output itself runs.

unnecessary_function.description: Flags a Function whose body is empty or just a single statement. An empty body does nothing, and a single statement is usually simple enough to inline at its call site instead. Events are never flagged, since they may deliberately forward to shared logic. A Native function is never flagged either, since it has no Papyrus body — the engine supplies the implementation. A Function named Fragment_<digits> (matched case-insensitively; a CreationKit-generated fragment entry point) is never flagged either, since the engine calls it directly and it isn't something the script's own author could inline away. A parameterless Function returning Int, Float, Bool, or String whose body is exactly one statement is never flagged either, since that shape is how a script exposes a named constant to the outside world without baking it into every instance as a Property/Variable; an empty body of that shape is still flagged, because it doesn't return a constant. The fix only handles a pure forwarding wrapper (its one statement is itself a call passing every one of its own parameters straight through, unchanged, to it), rewriting call sites to call the wrapped function directly; the wrapper's own declaration is left in place. An empty function is reported but not rewritten.

unknown_actor_value.description: Flags a call to an Actor Value function (GetActorValue, SetActorValue, ModActorValue, DamageActorValue, ...) whose Actor Value name isn't one of the target game's built-in ones, a strong sign of a typo. Only a plain string literal argument is checked. Disabled by default, since a project's own plugin can define custom Actor Values.

repeated_setoutfit.description: Flags a second SetOutfit(...) call passing the exact same outfit (and other arguments) as an earlier call on the same receiver, with nothing in between guaranteed to have changed what they're wearing, since a redundant repeated SetOutfit call is known to sometimes leave the actor with no visible equipment. Matches by the SetOutfit method name alone, case-insensitively, without resolving the receiver to an Actor.

place_at_me.description: Flags PlaceAtMe/PlaceActorAtMe calls whose returned reference is not stored, and PlaceAtMe calls that create multiple objects at once, because either pattern prevents reliable cleanup of every created object.

missing_doc_comment.description: Flags a ScriptName, Property, or Function/Event declaration with no {...} documentation comment on the line right after it. Disabled by default.

invalid_random_range.description: Flags, as an error, a Utility.RandomInt/RandomFloat call whose first argument isn't smaller than its second, since that never produces any actual randomness.

float_equality.description: Flags a direct == or != between two floats, since rounding error can make them compare unequal even when conceptually the same. Disabled by default.

missing_update_handler.description: Flags, as a warning, a RegisterForUpdate/RegisterForSingleUpdate/RegisterForUpdateGameTime/RegisterForSingleUpdateGameTime call with no matching OnUpdate/OnUpdateGameTime Event declared anywhere in the script, since the registration then has no effect. Disabled by default, since a matching Event declared on a script it Extends would otherwise be misreported as missing.

unused_import.description: Flags an Import statement whose script never has one of its Global functions called unqualified anywhere in this script. Only checked (and fixed) with project context.

event_signature_mismatch.description: Flags, as a warning, an Event declaration whose name matches one of the engine's own native events but whose parameter count/types don't match the signature it's actually called with, since a mismatched declaration still compiles but the engine then never invokes it correctly. Disabled by default, since the known-event list is a curated subset and matches by name alone.

circular_dependency.description: Flags a Property whose declared type, followed through that script's own Property declarations, eventually leads back to the script being linted (e.g. script A declaring a B Property while script B declares an A Property). A property typed as its own script isn't flagged. Disabled by default, since two scripts intentionally referencing each other for two-way communication is a common, legitimate design.

undefined_event.description: Warns about event handlers whose names are not defined anywhere in the script's ancestry, excluding engine-handled scripts and remote events.

boolean_simplification.description: Flags a Bool compared with == or != against true or false, since the value or its negation already says the same thing. The fix rewrites it to the value or '! value'.
